bull_bear.body:
- Integrated manufacturing model giving end-to-end control across design, manufacturing, quality assurance and delivery under one roof
- Design-led innovation: a 96-member in-house CAD team developing more than 400 new designs every month
- Long-standing partnerships with over 400 customers among major organised jewellery retailers, driving repeat business and revenue expansion from existing clients
- Over two decades of craftsmanship expertise in intricate 22KT CZ-studded gold jewellery
- Scalable manufacturing platform with sustained investment in infrastructure, technology and capacity expansion
- Multi-level quality control with inspections across critical production stages, BIS hallmarking and process traceability
- Strong balance sheet and operational execution — healthy ROCE, disciplined working capital management and timely execution
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Gold price volatility — Unprecedented fluctuations in gold prices may impact customer purchasing patterns, inventory valuation and working capital requirements. Heightened and fluctuating gold prices intensify working capital pressures across the sector, and management explicitly frames its outlook around prudently managing the impact of gold-price fluctuations on core profitability.
- Working-capital-intensive business model — Capacity expansion combined with elevated gold prices requires higher inventory levels and working capital, escalating financial demands. The Board also names working capital risk among the risks inherent to the gold jewellery manufacturing and trading sector.
- High dependence on the domestic market — A majority of revenue continues to be generated from the domestic market, limiting geographical diversification — a structural concentration the Company is trying to address through the Dubai subsidiary and an export strategy.
- Customer / concentration risk in a wholesale and job-work model — The Company operates primarily on a wholesale and job-work model serving organised jewellery retailers and wholesalers; the Board explicitly names concentration risk among the risks inherent to the sector and has put mitigation mechanisms in place.
- Moderate capacity utilisation against a large capacity build-out — Existing facilities are yet to harness their full potential, indicating the necessity for demand optimisation — a risk that grows as the Marol and Jaipur additions take total capacity towards nearly 7,900 kg per annum.
- Geopolitical, trade and regulatory risk on raw material and exports — Global uncertainties, modified import duties or trade disruptions can affect raw material procurement, exports and overall business performance. The industry remains externally dependent for raw materials, exposing it to global supply chain risks and foreign market volatility.
- Skilled labour shortage in the jewellery craft — The shortage of skilled labour, especially in the fragmented sector, arising from generational craftsmanship dependency, inadequate formal training and limited youth engagement, is among the industry's major concerns for a manufacturer whose product depends on artisan skill.
- Fashion-cycle and inventory obsolescence risk — Short-lived fashion trends and rapidly evolving global preferences challenge innovation and rapid adaptability, leading to inventory pressures and financial strain.
- Export demand weakness in key overseas markets — Global economic slowdown, particularly in key markets like the U.S., UAE and Hong Kong, has reduced export demand — directly relevant to the Company's stated international expansion plan.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company designs, develops and manufactures intricately crafted 22KT CZ (cubic-zirconia studded) casting gold jewellery for leading organised retailers and wholesalers, operating primarily on a wholesale and job-work model. Its portfolio spans bangles, rings, necklaces, jewellery sets and other occasion-specific jewellery for the wedding, festive and daily-wear segments, and it has recently forayed into machine-made plain gold jewellery, Mangalsutra and Turkish jewellery. Manufacturing is fully integrated, running from CAD design and prototyping through casting, stone setting, polishing, gold plating, BIS hallmarking, quality control, packaging and dispatch under one roof.

outlook.body:
- Broaden the product portfolio beyond core 22KT CZ casting jewellery into machine-made plain gold jewellery, Mangalsutra and Turkish jewellery to participate in new customer segments.
- Expand the manufacturing base — the newly commissioned Marol (Mumbai) facility and the upcoming Jaipur facility — to deepen relationships with existing customers, add new marquee accounts and support entry into newer markets.
- Strengthen presence in new domestic markets, particularly North India, while widening relationships with organised jewellery retailers.
- Pursue global expansion through the wholly owned Dubai subsidiary and a robust export strategy targeting markets such as the US, UK, Singapore and Malaysia.
- Prioritise stabilisation of core profitability amid gold-price fluctuations through consistent operational efficiency and disciplined execution.
- Invest in technology, manufacturing capabilities and operational efficiencies alongside continued emphasis on design innovation and execution excellence.
- Position the Company not merely as a large manufacturer but as a trusted, design-led benchmark for quality and craftsmanship for organised jewellery retailers in India and international markets.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Shanti Gold is in the middle of a three-site capacity build-out. It historically operated a single integrated facility at Andheri, Mumbai, commissioned in FY2023-24 with an installed capacity of 2,700 kg per annum. During FY2025-26 the Company announced the proposed expansion of a new manufacturing facility at Marol, Mumbai, adding approximately 4,000 kg per annum; commercial production at that Marol site (Plot No. 1, Compartment No. 5, Marol Co-operative Industrial Estate, Vasanji Road, Andheri East, Mumbai) commenced with effect from 08 June 2026, after the balance-sheet date. A third facility is being developed at Mahindra World City, Jaipur, on approximately three acres (around 50,000 square feet) of leasehold land acquired in 2018, which is stated to add 1,200 kg per annum of upcoming capacity. The Chairman states that these additions take total installed capacity to nearly 7,900 kg per annum once fully operational. Funding: IPO gross proceeds of Rs 360.11 crore included Rs 46.30 crore earmarked for capital expenditure on the proposed Jaipur facility, of which Rs 2.13 crore had been utilised as at 31 March 2026, leaving Rs 44.17 crore unutilised; a post-year-end Rights Issue allotted on 24 August 2026 infused Rs 99,83,46,265, to be applied primarily to working capital, with Acuite Ratings & Research Limited as Monitoring Agency. Beyond manufacturing, the Company incorporated a wholly owned Dubai subsidiary (Shanti Gold Jewellery Trading L.L.C. S.O.C., 13 May 2026) to support international business, and maintains branch offices across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural shift of Indian jewellery demand from the unorganised to the organised segment, aided by hallmarking, product certification and formalisation of retail, expanding the addressable customer base for organised manufacturing partners.
- Increasing outsourcing of manufacturing by organised jewellers, creating expansion opportunities with existing and emerging retail partners.
- Non-discretionary bridal demand: bridal jewellery is the largest segment of the Indian gold jewellery market and has shown steady growth despite elevated gold prices moderating purchase quantities.
- Growth in daily and fashion-wear jewellery driven by dynamic lifestyles, higher disposable incomes and younger consumers, favouring lightweight designs.
- Elevated gold prices shifting consumer preference to lighter-weight and lower-carat jewellery, prompting manufacturers to introduce lightweight collections that optimise gold utilisation.
- India's gems and jewellery market valued at USD 105.8 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 231.9 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 8.83% during 2026-2034 (IMARC).
- Management expects healthy volume growth in line with past performance, supported by accelerated capacity expansion, customer acquisitions and sustained market demand.
- Operating leverage: higher production capability from expanded capacity can improve manufacturing efficiency and support margin stability over the medium term.
- Export opportunity as international buyers increasingly seek reliable manufacturing partners offering quality assurance, design capabilities and scalable production, positioning Indian export-oriented manufacturers favourably.
- Rising penetration of digital retail, omnichannel distribution and design-led product innovation extending reach into Tier II and Tier III cities.
- Management cites a strong pipeline of customer additions supporting confidence in sustainable growth, but no quantified order book or pipeline value is disclosed in this annual report text.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Shanti Gold International Limited is an integrated Indian manufacturer of 22KT CZ-studded casting gold jewellery, established in 2003, supplying leading organised jewellery retailers and wholesalers across India and select international markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company designs, develops and manufactures intricately crafted 22KT CZ (cubic-zirconia studded) casting gold jewellery for leading organised retailers and wholesalers, operating primarily on a wholesale and job-work model. Its portfolio spans bangles, rings, necklaces, jewellery sets and other occasion-specific jewellery for the wedding, festive and daily-wear segments, and it has recently forayed into machine-made plain gold jewellery, Mangalsutra and Turkish jewellery. Manufacturing is fully integrated, running from CAD design and prototyping through casting, stone setting, polishing, gold plating, BIS hallmarking, quality control, packaging and dispatch under one roof.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Shanti Gold Jewellery Trading L.L.C. S.O.C. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in Dubai, United Arab Emirates on 13 May 2026, after the close of FY2025-26, to support the Company's international business; will be consolidated with effect from FY2026-27. The Company had no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company as on 31 March 2026.
- Utssav CZ Gold Jewels Limited — related party: Other listed entity in which Pankajkumar Jagawat (Chairman & Managing Director) and Shashank Jagawat (Non-Executive Director) hold directorships, as disclosed in the Corporate Governance Report directorships table.
- Share Samadhan Limited — related party: Other listed entity in which Independent Director Purvi Shah holds a directorship, as disclosed in the Corporate Governance Report directorships table.
- Ullu Digital Limited — related party: Other listed entity in which Independent Director Bhavika Ghuntla holds a directorship, as disclosed in the Corporate Governance Report directorships table.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **22KT CZ casting gold jewellery:** Bangles, Rings, Necklaces, Jewellery sets, Occasion-specific jewellery
- **New product categories:** Machine-made plain gold jewellery, Mangalsutra, Turkish jewellery

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Organised jewellery retailers and wholesalers in India
- Bridal / wedding gold jewellery segment
- Festive and daily / fashion wear jewellery segment
- Clients across 18 states and two Union Territories in India
- Four international markets, including the United Arab Emirates
- Key cities served: Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad
- Targeted export markets: US, UK, Singapore and Malaysia

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body: BIS hallmarking of every jewellery piece in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural shift of Indian jewellery demand from the unorganised to the organised segment, aided by hallmarking, product certification and formalisation of retail, expanding the addressable customer base for organised manufacturing partners.
- Increasing outsourcing of manufacturing by organised jewellers, creating expansion opportunities with existing and emerging retail partners.
- Non-discretionary bridal demand: bridal jewellery is the largest segment of the Indian gold jewellery market and has shown steady growth despite elevated gold prices moderating purchase quantities.
- Growth in daily and fashion-wear jewellery driven by dynamic lifestyles, higher disposable incomes and younger consumers, favouring lightweight designs.
- Elevated gold prices shifting consumer preference to lighter-weight and lower-carat jewellery, prompting manufacturers to introduce lightweight collections that optimise gold utilisation.
- India's gems and jewellery market valued at USD 105.8 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 231.9 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 8.83% during 2026-2034 (IMARC).
- Management expects healthy volume growth in line with past performance, supported by accelerated capacity expansion, customer acquisitions and sustained market demand.
- Operating leverage: higher production capability from expanded capacity can improve manufacturing efficiency and support margin stability over the medium term.
- Export opportunity as international buyers increasingly seek reliable manufacturing partners offering quality assurance, design capabilities and scalable production, positioning Indian export-oriented manufacturers favourably.
- Rising penetration of digital retail, omnichannel distribution and design-led product innovation extending reach into Tier II and Tier III cities.
- Management cites a strong pipeline of customer additions supporting confidence in sustainable growth, but no quantified order book or pipeline value is disclosed in this annual report text.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Broaden the product portfolio beyond core 22KT CZ casting jewellery into machine-made plain gold jewellery, Mangalsutra and Turkish jewellery to participate in new customer segments.
- Expand the manufacturing base — the newly commissioned Marol (Mumbai) facility and the upcoming Jaipur facility — to deepen relationships with existing customers, add new marquee accounts and support entry into newer markets.
- Strengthen presence in new domestic markets, particularly North India, while widening relationships with organised jewellery retailers.
- Pursue global expansion through the wholly owned Dubai subsidiary and a robust export strategy targeting markets such as the US, UK, Singapore and Malaysia.
- Prioritise stabilisation of core profitability amid gold-price fluctuations through consistent operational efficiency and disciplined execution.
- Invest in technology, manufacturing capabilities and operational efficiencies alongside continued emphasis on design innovation and execution excellence.
- Position the Company not merely as a large manufacturer but as a trusted, design-led benchmark for quality and craftsmanship for organised jewellery retailers in India and international markets.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Shanti Gold is in the middle of a three-site capacity build-out. It historically operated a single integrated facility at Andheri, Mumbai, commissioned in FY2023-24 with an installed capacity of 2,700 kg per annum. During FY2025-26 the Company announced the proposed expansion of a new manufacturing facility at Marol, Mumbai, adding approximately 4,000 kg per annum; commercial production at that Marol site (Plot No. 1, Compartment No. 5, Marol Co-operative Industrial Estate, Vasanji Road, Andheri East, Mumbai) commenced with effect from 08 June 2026, after the balance-sheet date. A third facility is being developed at Mahindra World City, Jaipur, on approximately three acres (around 50,000 square feet) of leasehold land acquired in 2018, which is stated to add 1,200 kg per annum of upcoming capacity. The Chairman states that these additions take total installed capacity to nearly 7,900 kg per annum once fully operational. Funding: IPO gross proceeds of Rs 360.11 crore included Rs 46.30 crore earmarked for capital expenditure on the proposed Jaipur facility, of which Rs 2.13 crore had been utilised as at 31 March 2026, leaving Rs 44.17 crore unutilised; a post-year-end Rights Issue allotted on 24 August 2026 infused Rs 99,83,46,265, to be applied primarily to working capital, with Acuite Ratings & Research Limited as Monitoring Agency. Beyond manufacturing, the Company incorporated a wholly owned Dubai subsidiary (Shanti Gold Jewellery Trading L.L.C. S.O.C., 13 May 2026) to support international business, and maintains branch offices across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated manufacturing model giving end-to-end control across design, manufacturing, quality assurance and delivery under one roof
- Design-led innovation: a 96-member in-house CAD team developing more than 400 new designs every month
- Long-standing partnerships with over 400 customers among major organised jewellery retailers, driving repeat business and revenue expansion from existing clients
- Over two decades of craftsmanship expertise in intricate 22KT CZ-studded gold jewellery
- Scalable manufacturing platform with sustained investment in infrastructure, technology and capacity expansion
- Multi-level quality control with inspections across critical production stages, BIS hallmarking and process traceability
- Strong balance sheet and operational execution — healthy ROCE, disciplined working capital management and timely execution
